ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: A student performed an experiment in which a butane lighter was fixed directly underwater below a 100 mL graduated cylinder, and the cylinder was filled with water. The lighter's switch was pressed, and butane gas $\ce{C4H10}$ was released into the graduated cylinder. The laboratory student's data are as follows: the mass before releasing the gas was 20.432g, the mass of the lighter after release was 20.296g, the volume of gas collected was 68.40 mL, the water temperature was 19.0°C, and the atmospheric pressure was 745 mmHg. Please determine the percent error of the student's result. (The final answer is a numerical value)

The laboratory student's data are as follows: the mass before releasing the gas was 20.432g, the mass of the lighter after release was 20.296g, the volume of gas collected was 68.40 mL, the water temperature was 19.0°C, and the atmospheric pressure was 745 mmHg. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a container filled with water, with a lighter below the water surface; above the lighter, an inverted graduated cylindrical measuring cylinder is placed, and gas can be collected in the measuring cylinder by the water displacement method. Therefore this apparatus corresponds to the experiment of “butane gas collected over water.” Reasoning: The mass before the lighter released gas was 20.432 g, and the mass after release was 20.296 g, so the experimentally measured butane mass loss is 20.432 - 20.296 = 0.136 g. Since the gas is collected over water, the water vapor pressure needs to be subtracted; at 19.0°C the water vapor pressure is about 16.5 mmHg, so the partial pressure of butane is 745 - 16.5 = 728.5 mmHg = 728.5/760 = 0.958 atm. The collected gas volume V = 68.40 mL = 0.06840 L, and the temperature T = 19.0 + 273.15 = 292.15 K. Using PV = nRT: n = (0.958)(0.06840)/(0.08206 × 292.15) ≈ 0.00273 mol. The molar mass of butane C4H10 is about 58.12 g/mol, so the butane mass calculated according to the gas law is 0.00273 × 58.12 ≈ 0.159 g. Percent error = |0.136 - 0.159| / 0.159 × 100% ≈ 14.5%.

raw_record.question_text: A student performed an experiment in which a butane lighter was fixed directly underwater below a 100 mL graduated cylinder, and the cylinder was filled with water. The lighter's switch was pressed, and butane gas $\ce{C4H10}$ was released into the graduated cylinder. The laboratory student's data are as follows: the mass before releasing the gas was 20.432g, the mass of the lighter after release was 20.296g, the volume of gas collected was 68.40 mL, the water temperature was 19.0°C, and the atmospheric pressure was 745 mmHg. Please determine the percent error of the student's result. (The final answer is a numerical value)

method.method_draft: From the image, identify the setup as butane gas collected over water in an inverted graduated cylinder. From the text, take initial lighter mass 20.432 g, final mass 20.296 g, collected gas volume 68.40 mL, water temperature 19.0°C, and atmospheric pressure 745 mmHg. Calculate the observed mass loss: 20.432 − 20.296 = 0.136 g. Correct the gas pressure for water vapor: P_C4H10 = 745 − P_H2O(19°C) ≈ 745 − 16.5 = 728.5 mmHg = 0.958 atm. Use V = 0.06840 L and T = 292.15 K in PV = nRT to find moles of butane, then convert to theoretical collected mass using M(C4H10) ≈ 58.12 g/mol. Finally compare the measured lighter mass loss to this gas-law mass with percent error = |experimental − theoretical|/theoretical × 100 to obtain 14.5%.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct experimental-vs-theoretical comparison route; it uses the diagram to identify the gas as collected over water, then uses Dalton’s law and the ideal gas law to compute the expected butane mass from the measured gas volume and compare it with the lighter mass loss.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the diagram first: a lighter is underwater beneath an inverted graduated cylinder filled with water, so the released butane is collected by water displacement and the collected gas is saturated with water vapor. The cylinder is open to the water bath, so the gas pressure should be treated as atmospheric pressure corrected for water vapor.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the written chemical formula C4H10 and all numerical measurements: 20.432 g before release, 20.296 g after release, 68.40 mL gas volume, 19.0°C water temperature, and 745 mmHg atmospheric pressure.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use Dalton’s law: P_butane = P_atm − P_H2O at 19.0°C, with water vapor pressure about 16.5 mmHg. Convert pressure to atm, volume to L, and temperature to K. Use PV = nRT to find moles of butane in the collected gas, then multiply by molar mass of C4H10, about 58.12 g/mol. Compute mass lost by the lighter as initial mass minus final mass. Percent error = |measured mass loss − gas-law mass| / gas-law mass × 100, which should give about 14.5.
